Stage 02

Statutory Formation & Board Resolutions

Competent registry, governing statute, capital lockup rules, and first board resolution template.

Competent corporate registry

Registro Mercantil Central (name certification) and Registro Mercantil Provincial de Madrid (constitutive inscription and corporate registration); registry oversight by the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública.

Governing statute

Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, de 2 de julio, por el que se aprueba el texto refundido de la Ley de Sociedades de Capital (Spanish Capital Companies Act); applicable Articles 1-23 (incorporation), 28-31 (registered office), 58-66 (corporate domicile), 89-99 (minimum share capital for Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada), 102-110 (participations), 209-213 (administrators), and 226-227 (first board resolutions); supplementary application of Royal Decree 1784/1996 (Mercantile Registry Regulations).

Formation / constitutional filings

Escritura pública de constitución (public deed of incorporation) executed before a Spanish notary, followed by mandatory inscription in the Registro Mercantil and publication in the Boletín Oficial del Registro Mercantil (BORME).

Incorporation processing time

⚡ 29 business days (SOP sum)

Paid-up Capital & Blocked Account Regime Mandatory Capital Deposit & Lockup

Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada requires minimum share capital of EUR 3,000, fully subscribed and fully paid in cash at incorporation; capital is divided into participaciones not negotiable securities. The full amount must be deposited into a blocked escrow account (cuenta restringida) at a Spanish credit institution before deed execution; the bank issues a deposit certificate, the funds remain blocked until registry inscription, and the certificate is cancelled post-registration.

Funding & unlock path: Fire safety: basic fire-prevention compliance under the Código Técnico de la Edificación and a fire-safety certificate (certificado de protección contra incendios) for any leased office premises. Structural load inspections: not applicable for non-industrial office use. Occupational clearance: completion of a risk-prevention assessment under Ley 31/1995, implementation of the company's accident-prevention plan, and registration with the Social Security authority before hiring any staff.

Paid-in capital rule: Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada requires minimum share capital of EUR 3,000, fully subscribed and fully paid in cash at incorporation; capital is divided into participaciones not negotiable securities. The full amount must be deposited into a blocked escrow account (cuenta restringida) at a Spanish credit institution before deed execution; the bank issues a deposit certificate, the funds remain blocked until registry inscription, and the certificate is cancelled post-registration.

Pro-Forma First Board Resolution Draft
That part of the subscribed capital of EUR 3,000 being fully subscribed and paid into the blocked account, the issuance of participations to each founding member is hereby approved. The registered office is fixed at Calle de Serrano 10, 28001 Madrid, within the jurisdiction of the Madrid Mercantile Registry, and adoption of this corporate seat is ratified. Don/Doña [Name] is appointed Sole Administrator with the powers granted by Article 62 of the Capital Companies Act, and Don/Doña [Name] is appointed Non-Member Secretary; both accept their offices. The Administrator is authorized to execute all filings before the Mercantile Registry, the State Tax Agency, the Official Gazette (BORME) and all other authorities to perfect incorporation.
Industrial Access / EIA & Civil Defense Approval Exempted / Not Required

No industrial licensing board applies to this financial private-equity SPV; sector oversight rests with the Comisión Nacional del Mercado de Valores (CNMV) and SEPBLAC for anti-money-laundering surveillance.

Category: None required — ISIC 6499 (other financial service activities) is not an industrial license category; only an optional municipal activity license (licencia de actividad) is triggered if a physical administrative office is opened in Spain.

Stage 03

Tax Identity & Indirect Tax

Tax authority e-portal, entity tax classification elections, VAT thresholds, and 0% export documentation chain.

Tax ID Application Infrastructure

Competent tax authority

Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) — Spanish Tax Agency; electronic portal: Sede Electrónica (sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es) providing access to Form 036 (census registration for CIT, IVA, and NIF), the SII web service, and the VIES validation tool

E-government filing portal

Foreign investors must execute a public incorporation deed before a Spanish notary, obtain a provisional NIF from AEAT (Form 036), file the deed at the Registro Mercantil, and then receive the definitive NIF (tax identification number serving simultaneously as the TIN for Corporate Income Tax and as NIF-IVA for VAT). The SL must be registered on the territorial census, designate a tax domicile, and (if non-EU shareholders are present) appoint a Spanish tax representative with sufficient power for tax compliance. Mandatory IVA registration (Form 036/037) is performed in the same census procedure, to be completed before any taxable supply is made in the IVA territory.

Tax ID type & application path: Entity_Level_Taxation — Foreign investors must execute a public incorporation deed before a Spanish notary, obtain a provisional NIF from AEAT (Form 036), file the deed at the Registro Mercantil, and then receive the definitive NIF (tax identification number serving simultaneously as the TIN for Corporate Income Tax and as NIF-IVA for VAT). The SL must be registered on the territorial census, designate a tax domicile, and (if non-EU shareholders are present) appoint a Spanish tax representative with sufficient power for tax compliance. Mandatory IVA registration (Form 036/037) is performed in the same census procedure, to be completed before any taxable supply is made in the IVA territory.

Default Tax Classification & Elections

Default tax classification

Entity_Level_Taxation

Available election forms

No U.S.-style check-the-box election exists under Spanish law; an SL is per se a fully taxable entity for Spanish Corporate Income Tax (Impuesto sobre Sociedades) at a 25% standard rate. Available statutory elections include: (i) optional tax-consolidation regime for a Spanish fiscal group (Arts. 56–70 LIS) covering 100%-held Spanish subsidiaries; (ii) neutrality/election for reorganizations under Art. 76 LIS (mergers, demergers, asset contributions/segregations); (iii) election of quarterly/semi-annual VAT refund filing (IVA mensual for large taxpayers); and (iv) tax-representative nomination. Hybrid mismatch neutralizing adjustments under ATAD are mandatory, not elective, except where the taxpayer may substantively elect alternative allocation or origination timing; any such election must be disclosed in the annual CIT return.

VAT / GST & 0% Export Zero-Rating

Standard VAT / GST rate

21%

Mandatory registration threshold (Nexus)

No economic-turnover de minimis threshold applies to established or non-established businesses performing taxable supplies in the Spanish IVA territory; any person carrying out such supplies must register with AEAT (Form 036) before commencement. For intra-Community distance selling and EU e-commerce sales to final consumers, the Union-wide EUR 10,000 threshold applies: below it, supplies remain taxable in the member state of origin; above it, registration or OSS (One Stop Shop) filing in Spain is required. A PE-buyout SPV that merely holds shares and receives dividends/lending interest has no IVA registration obligation, unless it invoices management, financing, or service fees (services to/from non-established persons may be shifted to the reverse-charge mechanism or subject to the place-of-supply-for-services rules).

Export 0% zero-rating conditions

Exports of goods to third countries and intra-Community dispatches to an IVA-identifiable customer (validated VIES VAT number) are exempt with the right to deduct input VAT (effective 0% rating) under Arts. 21 and 25 LIVA. The exporter must be the exporter of record in the customs territory, evidence physical dispatch/transport outside of Spain or to another member state, and hold the customs export declaration and transport documentation. Services directly related to export (international transport, loading/unloading, customs clearance, international brokerage) are likewise zero-rated under Art. 21 LIVA. For a PE-buyout SPV, zero-rating will generally be claimed only for onward sale of portfolio assets with physical export or for intra-Union services if the recipient is a taxable person in another member state; all conditions must be documented and retained; otherwise the supply is taxed in Spain at the applicable IVA rate (21% standard/10% reduced).

  • Customs Export Declaration (Single Administrative Document / DUA) accepted and released electronically by the EU customs IT system (Export Exit Release), evidencing the third-country destination and exporter of record
  • Transport document — Bill of Lading (B/L), CMR waybill, or Air Waybill issued to the Spanish exporter of record, proving physical dispatch and delivery outside the EU or into another member state
  • Commercial invoice and sales/purchase contract including Incoterms, quantity, price, and buyer's identity/VAT number (VIES validation printout required for intra-Union dispatches)
  • Inward Remittance Certificate — bank SWIFT MT103 or equivalent credit advice demonstrating payment receipt of the export consideration
  • Customs valuation evidence and any restricted/linked-good licenses or permits for the specific goods, where applicable

Mandatory B2B electronic invoicing under Law 18/2022 (Ley Crea y Crece), implemented by Royal Decree 1008/2023, requires issuance, transmission, and receipt of structured e-invoices (Facturae or PEPPOL-compliant formats) for all transactions between Spanish businesses. The SII (Suministro Inmediato de Información) imposes near-real-time reporting of issuance and received invoices to AEAT through web services/APIs (XML) within 4 working days of issue (8 for receipts), applicable to taxpayers with annual turnover exceeding EUR 6,000,000 and to those VAT-group registered. The Veri*Factu system (phased in from 2025) will require qualified billing-management systems to generate a secure QR/digital stamp over each invoice record to guarantee integrity and visibility to AEAT; failing to transmit SII/Veri*Factu data is penalized as a formal-tax-infringement with fines up to EUR 2,000 per invoice record.

AEAT may retroactively disallow export zero-rating where the documentary bundle is incomplete or contradictory, assessing the unreported VAT at 21% plus late-payment interest for the ordinary 4-year limitation period (extended to 5 years for large-enterprise taxpayers from 2025) without prejudice to criminal proceedings. Fraudulent or abusive claims attract penalties ranging from 50% (minor infraction) to 150% (deliberate fraud or resistance to inspection) under Arts. 191–194 of Law 58/2003 (LGT), together with loss of deduction rights and prohibition on participating in SII/Veri*Factu schemes. Where the annual defrauded amount exceeds EUR 120,000, criminal tax fraud under Art. 305 of the Código Penal applies, with imprisonment of 1–6 years, fines of up to six times the defrauded amount, and disqualification from tax benefits/public subsidies; retrospective clawback and penalty assessment may include subordinate entities for organized falsification of export documentation.

Stage 04

Banking & Treasury Architecture

Central-bank FX diagnosis, tier-1 local banks vs offshore digital EMI matrix, and KYC rejection defense guide.

Foreign Exchange Regime & Central Bank Policy

Current-account convertibility

Spain has full current and capital account convertibility as a euro-area member state. The euro is freely convertible; no prior exchange-control authorization is required for capital contributions, dividend remittances, trade settlements, or intercompany treasury flows. Profit remittance from an SL is subject to corporate income tax and non-resident dividend withholding tax (generally 19% absent treaty relief) but is not subject to FX approval. The only material frictions are institutional KYC/AML documentation, OECD/EU transparency filings, foreign investment statistical declarations, and Modelo 720 asset reporting thresholds for non-Spanish accounts.

Export proceeds surrender rules

Spain imposes no mandatory export proceeds surrender regime. There is no statutory timeline enforced by the central bank, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no requirement to repatriate export receivables into Spain. Export proceeds may remain in foreign-currency accounts of a Spanish resident company, provided that balance-of-payments and tax/AML reporting obligations are met. Intra-EU trade and third-country transactions are subject only to standard commercial invoicing and suspicious-transaction reporting rules.

Central bank supervision: Banco de España (Bank of Spain), together with the Dirección General de Comercio Internacional e Inversiones of the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Business as the competent foreign exchange and foreign investment statistical control authority

Offshore Digital Bank / EMI Whitelist

Cross-border EMI / Fintech rails Fit: High

Legally viable only for EU-licensed electronic money institutions (EMIs) and payment institutions passporting into Spain under Directive 2009/110/EC and Directive (EU) 2015/2366. Practical feasibility for a leveraged buyout SPV is generally Low-to-Medium because most digital EMIs decline complex private-equity holding structures, impose sub-limits, and cannot provide intragroup lending facilities. A digital EMI may be used for operating expenses and minor trade payments, but the core escrow and syndicated-loan treasury should sit with a tier-1 Spanish credit institution.

Core KYC Rejection Triggers & Defense Dossier

Newly incorporated SPV with no operating history and no audited financial statements

Root cause: Newly incorporated SPV with no operating history and no audited financial statements

Defense evidence: Certificate of incorporation and bylaws of ES_SL; NIF/CIF tax identification; notarized board resolution appointing signatories and declaring investment purpose; detailed business plan for the LBO transaction; term sheet or equity commitment letter from the PE fund; parent fund KYC pack including constitutional documents, fund prospectus, regulatory license, and audited financial statements.
Complex multi-jurisdictional ownership chain involving offshore holding companies and Latin American investors

Root cause: Complex multi-jurisdictional ownership chain involving offshore holding companies and Latin American investors

Defense evidence: Full organizational chart from ultimate natural-person beneficial owners to ES_SL; registry extracts or equivalent certification for each intermediate holding entity; source-of-funds file for the equity commitment; notarized declarations of source of wealth; evidence that all intermediate entities have economic substance and are tax compliant in their respective domiciles.
Use of shareholder loans combined with third-party leverage creating suspicion of opaque debt financing

Root cause: Use of shareholder loans combined with third-party leverage creating suspicion of opaque debt financing

Defense evidence: Signed intercompany loan agreements with market terms; evidence that shareholder loans are recorded in the statutory accounts; bank statements of the lending entity; ECB/FX statistical declarations where applicable; pipeline transaction documents showing acquisition target, purchase price, and debt-to-equity ratio.
Substantial non-EU wire movements from Brazil, Mexico, or other LATAM jurisdictions into the SPV

Root cause: Substantial non-EU wire movements from Brazil, Mexico, or other LATAM jurisdictions into the SPV

Defense evidence: Source-of-wealth letters from the remitting bank; notarized investor resolutions; chain of title to the injected funds; certificates of good standing of the foreign PE vehicle; evidence that inbound investments are registered with Spain's Register of Foreign Investments; correspondent-bank references for the remitting institutions.
UBO or director appearing on PEP, sanctions, or adverse-media watchlists

Root cause: UBO or director appearing on PEP, sanctions, or adverse-media watchlists

Defense evidence: Independent and dated PEP/sanctions screening report from a recognized provider; legal explanation of the screening result if a partial name match arises; official public records or court certificates proving dismissal or non-materiality of adverse media; documented rationale for the commercial legitimacy of the SPV's acquisition mandate.

Cross-Border Clearing Corridors & Settlement Fit

For euro-denominated capital injections from EU investors or the PE fund, the primary clearing rail is SEPA Credit Transfer using IBAN, with purpose code EQUI or INVE and a clear remittance narrative identifying the SPV NIF/CIF, the capital increase or shareholder loan date, and the underlying acquisition deal. For non-euro or extra-EEA transactions, SWIFT MT103 is mandatory, with field 70 referencing the LBO pipeline and field 50K/52D showing the contributing entity. The corporate bank will perform a pre-credit compliance check requiring source-of-funds documentation and the notarial certificate of capital increase or loan agreement. After closing, a post-investment statistical foreign-investment declaration must be filed electronically with the Dirección General de Comercio Internacional e Inversiones when the non-resident acquires 10% or more of the SL capital or when the transaction exceeds the applicable reporting threshold.For euro payments to Spanish and EEA suppliers, use SEPA Credit Transfer via TARGET2-Banco de España. For non-EEA, non-euro trade settlements, use SWIFT MT103 with supporting commercial invoice and transport documents. For trade finance against Latin American or other third-country counterparties, issue irrevocable documentary letters of credit via MT700/MT710 or collection instructions via MT400; conditional guarantees and standby LCs use MT760. Any outbound disbursement related to the buyout, including settlement payments, intercompany loans, advisory fees, or the final acquisition consideration, must reference the transaction ID and comply with dual-use export controls, FDI rules of the target jurisdiction, and the bank's payment screening policies.Outright deliverable FX forwards (EUR/USD, EUR/MXN, EUR/BRL) with licensed counterparties under ISDA or local master agreementsFX swaps (swap de divisas) for short-term liquidity rotation between EUR and LATAM currenciesCross-currency swaps (XCCY) for converting fixed-rate debt obligations into EUR liabilitiesNon-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for restricted Latin American currencies such as ARS, CLP, COP, and PEN where onshore deliverability is unavailable to the SPV

E-commerce / gateway settlement fit: Legally viable only for EU-licensed electronic money institutions (EMIs) and payment institutions passporting into Spain under Directive 2009/110/EC and Directive (EU) 2015/2366. Practical feasibility for a leveraged buyout SPV is generally Low-to-Medium because most digital EMIs decline complex private-equity holding structures, impose sub-limits, and cannot provide intragroup lending facilities. A digital EMI may be used for operating expenses and minor trade payments, but the core escrow and syndicated-loan treasury should sit with a tier-1 Spanish credit institution.

Statutory filing calendar, progressive late penalties, external audit triggers, and statutory registers.

Statutory Filing Calendar

Statutory deliverableDeadline window Government feeDelinquency sanctions
Annual Accounts Deposit (Depósito de Cuentas Anuales) No later than July 30 for calendar-year companies; must be filed within one month after approval of the annual accounts, which must be approved by June 30. $15 USD Late filing triggers registry closure (cierre registral), financial penalties from approximately EUR 6 to EUR 60,000, and the company cannot validly file other corporate acts until the accounts are deposited; continued non-deposit for three consecutive years can lead to administrative dissolution and strike-off of the company.
Corporate Income Tax Return (Modelo 200) and Alternative Minimum Tax/Local Surcharge Calculations Within 25 days following the six-month period after the tax year end; for a December 31 fiscal year end, filing must occur by July 25. $0 USD Late filing penalties: surcharge of 1% plus late interest for each month of delay up to 12 months, and 15% plus late interest for delays exceeding 12 months; tax assessment and collection proceedings, asset freezes, and administrative fines up to EUR 20,000 for formal violations can apply.
Annual UBO Registry Updating Declaration (Declaración Anual de Actualización de Titulares Reales) Filing due within one month after any change in ultimate beneficial ownership, and in all cases an annual declaration must be filed together with the annual accounts deposit by July 30. $15 USD Monetary penalties under the AML framework for failure to keep UBO records and update the registry; registry closure prevents filing of subsequent corporate acts; possible sanctioning of directors and administrative fines up to EUR 60,000 for serious non-compliance.
Annual return deadline

No later than July 30 for calendar-year companies; must be filed within one month after approval of the annual accounts, which must be approved by June 30.

Statutory government annual fee

$15 USD

Late filing penalties

Late filing triggers registry closure (cierre registral), financial penalties from approximately EUR 6 to EUR 60,000, and the company cannot validly file other corporate acts until the accounts are deposited; continued non-deposit for three consecutive years can lead to administrative dissolution and strike-off of the company.

Strike-off trigger

Mandatory Audit Threshold Mandatory Audit for All Entities

Turnover: Independent audit is mandatory for an SL if, on two consecutive balance sheet dates, it meets two of three thresholds: total assets above EUR 2.85 million, net annual revenue above EUR 5.7 million, or average workforce above 50 employees; parent companies and certain holding structures are also audited regardless of size.
